title: Zephyr Games — Account research & outbound scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick internal scratchpad for outbound motion to Zephyr Games (mid-size multiplayer mobile studio, headquartered in Toronto). Goal: get intro with Head of Ops / Engineering to pitch Redwood Dedicated + Private for latency-sensitive multiplayer inference (in-game chat moderation, real-time personalization).

Account snapshot (public + inferred):
- Founded 2016, ~120 employees (60 eng), top titles: DriftRally, NeonSkies (live ops, 3M MAU combined).
- Monetization: free-to-play, live events + cosmetic store. Heavy focus on retention and real-time features.
- Recent news (Dec 2024): raised Series B, announced new real-time crossplay feature; press mentions push for lower latency and regional servers in APAC.
- Likely infra: mixed cloud + edge POC (GCP + small edge partners). In-house matchmaking + some serverless functions for event processing.

Why Redwood might land (value props to highlight):
- Latency-sensitive inference: continuous batching + KV cache reduces tail latency for short-turn chat moderation calls (use case: banned-word detection + toxicity signal mid-match).
- Hybrid deployment model: Dedicated pools for predictable throughput during events + Private/VPC for compliance and control of telemetry.
- Cost controls: batching/quantization recommendations can materially reduce token cost vs naive cloud LLM hosting — good for high-volume in-game personalization RPCs.
- Observability: per-route token/latency dashboards + regression alerts valuable for live ops teams during events with variable traffic.

Potential hooks / experiments to propose:
- 2-week POC: Hosted API for a single moderation route (mirror existing pipeline) to show latency + accuracy vs current service. Deliverables: latency distribution, cost per 100k requests, false-positive/negative summary for curated test set.
- Dedicated burst window: commit a small Dedicated pool for weekend live event; measure tail latency under real load.
- Private deployment feasibility study: HLD of VPC integration and kms requirements for customer data.

Key stakeholders (target personas & surfaces):
- Head of Engineering (Samir Patel) — cares about reliability, latency, infra cost.
- Director Live Ops (Anna Lopez) — cares about moderation, real-time personalization, and measurement.
- Principal Backend Eng (CTO org) — will evaluate SDK, integration steps, fallback policies.
- Security lead / infra compliance — KMS, audit logs, and VPC peering.

Outreach sequence (initial hypothesis):
1) Short LinkedIn + brief email to Samir (focus: "helping spikes during live events without overprovisioning")
2) If no reply: one-pager + case study email showing a similar customer (anonymized) improvement in cost/latency
3) Warm intro ask to Anna (live ops) with concrete question: "Have you measured moderation latency impact on retention during events?"

Email draft A (to Samir) — short and flexible: 
Subject: Reducing latency & infra cost during NeonSkies live events
Hi Samir — quick note: congrats on the Series B and the crossplay rollout. We helped a live-game studio cut moderation tail latency by ~40% and reduce per-request inference cost through batching + dedicated pools. Curious if you'd be open to a 20-min call to compare approaches before your next event?

Email draft B (to Anna) — technical & operational: 
Subject: Quick question on moderation latency during live events
Anna — is your team seeing moderation calls as a retention risk during high-concurrency events? We run a short POC that surfaces latency distribution and actionable batching configs — 2 weeks, low lift. Want me to connect you to our infra engineer for a quick tech call?

Objection handling (anticipated):
- "We already have an in-house moderation model": Ask about maintenance cost and peak scaling pain; propose hybrid (run cheap rules in-house, Redwood for scale + quality). Offer benchmark on cost vs ops time.
- "Security / data residency concerns": Outline Private + VPC option, KMS integration, audit logs; offer NDA and architecture sketch.
- "Vendor lock-in": Emphasize model/version pinning, canary rollouts, and exportable logs; highlight unified API to switch variants.

Technical notes to prep with Eng team (Ethan/Sofia follow-ups):
- Need sample traffic profile (qps, typical request size, 95/99 latency currently). Try to get a CSV or telemetry snapshot.
- Prepare a short eval prompt set for moderation + personalization KPI measurement.
- Cost model ask: current monthly inference spend estimate + expected event spike multiplier.
- Integration paths: REST API (fast), WebSocket streaming (if they need streaming chat moderation), SDK examples in Unity/Unreal wrappers.

Ask list for discovery call:
- What endpoints are latency-sensitive today (ms targets)?  p50/p95/p99 goals?
- Current infra topology for inference (in-house vs third-party)?
- Privacy/data residency requirements (EU/APAC customers)?
- Typical request size and rate during peak events?
- Who owns instrumentation/alerts for feature regressions?

Risks & unknowns:
- They may have long procurement timelines post-Series B. Need internal champion in Live Ops to run a POC quickly.
- Integration complexity if they rely on custom game-engine plugins for server-side logic.

Immediate next steps (this doc owner):
- [ ] Send Samir email, copy Anna, mention 2-week POC idea (target: this week).
- [ ] Slack Ethan to prepare sample prompt set + small eval harness.
- [ ] Draft short NDA/one-pager and attach to follow-up.
- [ ] Pull a short anonymized case study to reference in email 2.

Notes to self / quick heuristics:
- Keep first outreach low-friction: emphasise "compare approaches" not "buy".
- Use concrete numbers (latency %, cost per 100k) in follow-ups — engineers respond to specifics.
- If they ask about edge footprint, propose mixed Dedicated + near-edge (APAC) routing while we run canary in-hosted.

Conversation snippets to remember (for calls):
- "We can run the same moderation prompts against your baseline and show delta in 48 hours."
- "Dedicated pools are billed predictably and let you avoid overprovisioning during events."
- "We’ll keep your model versions pinned so rolling back is trivial if quality regresses."

End of scratchpad.
